files.purpose: Defines the whole macOS menu bar command set for Droppy Code as a SwiftUI `Commands` struct: it replaces the stock Settings, Save and New groups, empties .saveItem so File's Close cannot steal the Archive thread chord, injects Toggle sidebar / Command palette / Toggle terminal / Toggle changes / Toggle activity view after the View sidebar group, adds a top-level "Thread" menu with 9 numbered thread shortcuts, and replaces Help with a single Welcome tour item.
state_owned: let model: AppModel (injected reference, not owned by this struct)
private let shortcuts = ShortcutStore.shared (shared singleton reference)
side_effects: Opens the Settings window via WindowManager.shared.showSettings()
Brings the main window forward via WindowManager.shared.showMain()
Presents the welcome tour via Tour.present(model:)
Creates a git worktree indirectly via model.newThread(workspace: .worktree)
Launches a project script in a terminal indirectly via model.runScript(_:threadID:)
Opens a modal NSOpenPanel indirectly through model.chooseProjectFolder()
Creates a ThreadRuntime on demand, because `runtime` resolves through model.runtime(for:)
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI Commands / CommandGroup / CommandMenu scene DSL, which is the macOS menu bar
CommandGroupPlacement values .appSettings, .saveItem, .windowArrangement, .newItem, .sidebar, .help are AppKit menu-bar placements
.keyboardShortcut(KeyEquivalent(Character(String(number))), modifiers: .command) relies on the Command modifier

Comment records that File's stock Close sits before the Thread menu and would take the Cmd+W that Archive thread wants, so .saveItem is replaced with an empty group; secondary windows close on Cmd+W themselves (SecondaryWindow)
withAnimation wrapping a model mutation makes SwiftUI rebuild the menu bar commands on the main actor
ui_elements: Button "Settings\u2026" replacing .appSettings, shortcut from .openSettings
CommandGroup(replacing: .saveItem) {} - deliberately empty, removing the stock Close/Save items
Button titled AppInfo.name placed before .windowArrangement, shortcut .showMainWindow, followed by Divider()
CommandGroup(replacing: .newItem): "New thread" (.newThread), "New thread in worktree" (.newWorktreeThread), Divider(), "Add project\u2026" (.addProject)

CommandGroup(after: .sidebar): "Toggle sidebar" (.toggleSidebar), "Command palette" (.commandPalette), "Toggle terminal" (.toggleTerminal), "Toggle changes" (.toggleChanges), "Toggle activity view" (.toggleActivityView), Divider()

CommandMenu("Thread") with: "Stop", "Queue a chat", "Toggle plan mode", Divider(), "Previous thread", "Next thread", the run-script button, Thread 1 through Thread 9, Divider(), the finish button, "Archive thread\u2026", and the settle/reopen button
Run-script button title: model.topScript.map { "Run \(script.name)" } ?? "Run top script"
ForEach(1...9, id: \.self) producing Button "Thread \(number)" bound to Cmd+1 through Cmd+9
Settle button title: "Reopen thread" when model.selectedThread?.isSettled == true, otherwise "Settle thread"
Finish button title comes from model.finishActionTitle ("Settle thread", "Archive thread" or "Reopen thread")
CommandGroup(replacing: .help) with one Button "Welcome tour"
feature_notes: "Toggle terminal" and "Toggle changes" are both .disabled(model.selectedThreadID == nil)
"Stop" is disabled unless a turn is running: .disabled(!(runtime?.isRunning ?? false))

"Queue a chat" is disabled when the draft is empty OR the thread has pending approvals: .disabled((runtime?.draftIsEmpty ?? true) || !(runtime?.approvals.isEmpty ?? true)). The comment explains the approve button ships the same Cmd+Return and a menu command always wins over a button shortcut, so the queue would swallow the chord the approval card is asking for; with nothing to queue behind, the draft just goes out via queueDraftAsFollowUp.
"Toggle plan mode" flips the thread's interactionMode: $0.interactionMode = $0.interactionMode == .plan ? .build : .plan, and is disabled when no thread is selected
"Toggle activity view" runs inside withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide) while toggling model.settings.sidebarActivityView
The run-script item only fires when both model.topScript and model.selectedThreadID are non-nil, and is .disabled(model.topScript == nil)
The settle/reopen item is .disabled(model.selectedThread.map { $0.isHelper } ?? true), so helpers and an empty selection cannot be settled
"Archive thread\u2026" and the finish item are both disabled when selectedThreadID is nil
`runtime` is resolved freshly on each access as model.selectedThreadID.map(model.runtime(for:)), which creates the runtime if none exists yet
unresolved_questions: ShortcutStore's default key equivalents per ShortcutAction are not in this file, so the actual chords beyond Cmd+1 through Cmd+9 cannot be stated from here
Whether CommandGroup(before: .windowArrangement) lands the AppInfo.name button in the Window menu on every supported macOS version is not asserted anywhere in this file

files.purpose: The NSApplicationDelegate plus UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate for Droppy Code: it sequences launch (show main window, open a thread, welcome tour after 700 ms, bootstrap, background update checks, post-install About celebration), defers quit while a Hydra merge is running with a 4 minute cap, saves and tears down on terminate, and routes notification presentation and taps back to the right thread.
key_symbols: final class AppDelegate: NSObject, NSApplicationDelegate, UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate (@MainActor)
state_owned: var model: AppModel? - the delegate's handle on the app model, assigned from WindowManager.shared.model during applicationDidFinishLaunching
side_effects: Sets UNUserNotificationCenter.current().delegate = self at launch
Starts async Tasks: WebsiteCaptures.run(model:), the tour timer, AppModel.bootstrap(), and the terminate wait loop
Sleeps 700 milliseconds (Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(700))) before presenting the welcome tour
Starts background update checks via UpdateChecker.shared.startBackgroundChecks()
Consumes the updater's relaunch marker, arms the celebration and opens Settings on the About page
Writes the library and every unsaved thread document synchronously through model.saveBeforeQuit() on terminate
Flushes the token ledger's live spend on terminate (TokenLedger.shared.flushLiveSpend())
Terminates every MCP server the hub started (MCPHub.terminateAll()) on terminate
Polls every 250 milliseconds while a Hydra merge runs, up to Date.now + 4 * 60 seconds, then calls sender.reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate: true)
Activates the app (NSApp.activate()) and selects a thread when a notification is tapped
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSApplicationDelegate lifecycle: applicationDidFinishLaunching, applicationShouldHandleReopen, applicationShouldTerminate with .terminateNow / .terminateLater plus sender.reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate:), applicationWillTerminate
UserNotifications framework: UNUserNotificationCenter, UNNotification, UNNotificationResponse, UNNotificationPresentationOptions [.banner, .sound]
NSApp.isActive and the no-argument NSApp.activate()
macOS Dock reopen semantics through applicationShouldHandleReopen(_:hasVisibleWindows:)
Swift concurrency: a @MainActor class with nonisolated async delegate callbacks that hop back via await MainActor.run
persisted_fields: notification userInfo key "threadID" : String holding a UUID uuidString, read in both notification callbacks
notification userInfo key "update" : presence alone marks an update notification (userInfo["update"] != nil)
settings key hasSeenTour, read through model.settings.hasSeenTour, gates the welcome tour
the updater's relaunch marker, consumed by AppUpdater.shared.consumeRelaunchMarker() (its storage lives elsewhere)
ui_elements: Main window shown at launch through WindowManager.shared.showMain()
Welcome tour presented 700 ms after launch when settings.hasSeenTour is false
Settings window opened on page .about after an install relaunch and after tapping an update notification
Notification presentation options [.banner, .sound] by default, or [] (silent, no banner) when the notified thread is the selected one while NSApp.isActive
feature_notes: WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled short-circuits the entire normal launch: it starts Task { await WebsiteCaptures.run(model:) } and returns before showMain, openThreadOnLaunch, the tour, bootstrap, update checks and the relaunch marker. This is a capture/screenshot harness path, not the normal shipped launch.
applicationShouldHandleReopen reopens the main window only when hasVisibleWindows is false, and always returns true

Quit is deferred (.terminateLater) only while model.isAnyHydraMergeRunning; the wait is capped at 4 * 60 seconds with 250 ms polls, after which the app terminates anyway. Comment: the merge is a minute or two of git and one model call, and losing it half-way leaves the work unmerged until the user's next message.
With no model or no running merge, applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateNow immediately
willPresent returns [] for a notification whose threadID equals the selected thread while NSApp.isActive, so an already-open chat gets no duplicate banner; every other case gets [.banner, .sound]

didReceive: a non-update notification shows the main window, then selects the thread from userInfo["threadID"] and activates the app; an update notification skips showMain and instead opens Settings on the .about page after activating
Terminate ordering is exactly: model?.saveBeforeQuit(), then TokenLedger.shared.flushLiveSpend(), then MCPHub.terminateAll()
unresolved_questions: WebsiteCaptures is referenced but defined elsewhere, so whether it is compiled into release builds or gated behind a build flag cannot be decided from this file

The notification request identifier equals the thread's uuidString (set in AppModel.notify), which implies one pending notification per thread; this file never removes delivered notifications, so where that happens is not visible here

files.purpose: The central @MainActor @Observable library model: it owns the projects and threads arrays plus a fine-grained ObservedValue cell system (project cells, thread cells, child cells, selection cells) so a write to one thread does not re-render the whole sidebar, and implements project and thread CRUD, sidebar ordering and drag reordering, helper/sub-agent spawning, idle runtime release, git worktree creation, notifications and the dock badge, text-generation engine selection, and debounced plus synchronous library persistence. It also declares AppAlert and the ProjectFile reader for droppy-code.json scripts.
key_symbols: struct AppAlert: Identifiable { let id = UUID(); var title: String; var message: String }
private struct AppModel.ThreadIndex { positions: [UUID: Int]; projects: [UUID: [Int]] }
struct AppModel.FinishRequest: Equatable { let id = UUID(); let threadID: UUID; let reopens: Bool }
struct AppModel.ArchiveRequest: Equatable { let id = UUID(); let threadID: UUID }
enum ProjectFile { static func scripts(at:) -> [ProjectScript]; static func symbol(for:) -> String }
private static func sync<Value: Identifiable & Equatable>(_:with:)
calls_into: ThreadRuntime.stopSession() / saveNow() / cancelPersistence() / holdsOnlyPersistedState / isRunning / ensureLoaded() / snapshotForPersistence() / installContinuation(_:) / unsavedSnapshot() / enqueueFollowUp(text:attachments:) / send() / draft / interrupt() / isLoadingHistory / turns / continuation / followUps / isTerminalVisible
Git(_:) with isRepository(), hasCommits(), status(), addWorktree(at:branch:base:), removeWorktree(at:), deleteCheckpoints(thread:)

hydraPickerPairs, hydraLead(of:for:), sweepHydraCopies(), resumeHydraMerges(), releaseHydraCopy(of:), runningDroppyHeads(of:), finishHydraHead(_:status:summary:), hydraHeadTurnFinished(_:status:), isAnyHydraMergeRunning
providers.status(_:), refreshAll(), loadCatalog(_:), defaultModel(for:), executable(for:), environment(for:)

settings.isEnabled(_:), settings.preference(for:model:), settings.lastEffort(for:), settings.defaultProvider, settings.defaultRuntimeMode, settings.defaultWorkspaceMode, settings.hydraEnabled, settings.lastHydraPairID, settings.lastProjectID, settings.threadFinishAction, settings.settleSound, settings.chimeWhenFinished, settings.notifyWhenFinished, settings.textGeneration
state_owned: let settings: AppSettings, let providers: ProviderRegistry, let mcp: MCPStore, let terminals: TerminalStore, let sidebar: SidebarLayout
@ObservationIgnored private(set) var autoContinue: AutoContinue! (implicitly unwrapped, built after self exists)
@ObservationIgnored var hydraHeadRetries: [UUID: Int] = [:] - how often each Droppy-run head has been restarted after failing at the door; a head gets two more goes
private(set) var projects: [Project] = [] with a didSet that syncs projectCells
private(set) var threads: [ChatThread] = [] with a didSet that syncs threadCells and childCells and rebuilds ThreadIndex only when membership or project assignment changed

var selectedThreadID: UUID? with a didSet that flips selection cells, marks the thread and its children read on the next main-actor tick, records SwitchLatency, schedules the idle session stop for the thread being left, warms neighbors and remembers the last project
var sidebarRevealThreadID: UUID? - never persisted, nil at rest
var finishRequest: FinishRequest?, var archiveRequest: ArchiveRequest?
side_effects: Reads the library from disk at init via Storage.loadLibrary() and rewrites running statuses
Debounced library write: scheduleSave() sleeps 400 milliseconds, then DiskWriter.shared.encodeAndWrite(library, to: Storage.libraryURL)
Immediate library writes (saveLibrary()) on settle, reopen, delete and deleteArchivedThreads

saveBeforeQuit() disables persistence, cancels the save task, writes the library synchronously, cancels persistence and stops the session on every runtime, writes each runtime's unsavedSnapshot() to Storage.threadURL(threadID), waits for queued writes, then terminals.terminateAll()

Launches Tasks in bootstrap(): document prefetch, settings.loadKeychainInBackground(), LoginEnvironment.load(), sweepHydraCopies(), resumeHydraMerges(), a repeating merge sweep every 300 seconds, providers.refreshAll(), parallel catalog loads, and Storage.sweepOrphanedAttachments()
Per-thread idle session stop tasks that sleep 600 seconds in a loop, then stopSession() and releaseIdleRuntime()
git subprocess work through Git.addWorktree, Git.removeWorktree and Git.deleteCheckpoints
Opens a modal NSOpenPanel in addProjectsFromPanel()
Requests notification authorization ([.alert, .sound, .badge]) once, and posts UNNotificationRequests
Sets NSApp.dockTile.badgeLabel and calls NSApp.requestUserAttention(.informationalRequest)
Plays SettleChime and FinishChime
Deletes thread documents and closes terminal sessions (Storage.deleteDocument/deleteDocuments, terminals.closeAll)
Reads droppy-code.json from a project folder in ProjectFile.scripts(at:)
Spawns agent processes indirectly through ThreadRuntime.send()
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSOpenPanel with canChooseDirectories, canChooseFiles, allowsMultipleSelection, prompt, message and runModal()
AppKit NSApp.isActive, NSApp.requestUserAttention(.informationalRequest) and NSApp.dockTile.badgeLabel for the dock unread badge
UserNotifications: UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization(options:), UNMutableNotificationContent, UNNotificationRequest with a nil trigger
SwiftUI withAnimation plus the Observation framework (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored)
Unix-style paths: URL.standardizedFileURL.path and worktree paths joined under Storage.worktreesDirectory
git worktrees on a POSIX checkout, with branch names of the form droppy-code/<8 hex chars>

Swift exclusivity: the sync/write split exists because a cell write inside withAnimation makes SwiftUI rebuild the menu bar commands on the spot, which reads thread(_:) and would trap if the cell dictionary were still borrowed
persisted_fields: Library { projects: [Project], threads: [ChatThread] } written to Storage.libraryURL
settings.lastProjectID (UUID?) set by rememberLastProject and cleared when the project is missing or removed

ChatThread fields written here: lastStatus, updatedAt, hasUnread, isArchived, isPinned, isSettled, settledAt, activityOrder, activityOrderDay, sortOrder, projectID, worktreePath, branch, providerSessionID, providerResumeAt, title, hasCustomTitle, foldsHelpers, isInPanel, parentThreadID, interactionMode, provider, model, effort, fastMode, runtimeMode, hydraPairID, hydraEnabled, hydra.status, hydra.finishedAt
Project fields written here: name, path, scripts, isExpanded
Project script file droppy-code.json at the project root, with array field "scripts" of objects { "name": String, "command": String, "icon": String?, "runOnWorktreeCreate": Bool defaulting to false }
Notification userInfo ["threadID": threadID.uuidString], notification request identifier = threadID.uuidString
ui_elements: NSOpenPanel prompt "Add project", message "Choose a folder for your agents to work in."
AppAlert title "Worktree unavailable", message "New worktrees need a git repository with at least one commit."
AppAlert title "Could not create a worktree", message error.localizedDescription
Forwarded thread title: "Continued: " + source title, with hasCustomTitle = true

finishActionTitle: "Reopen thread" when settings.threadFinishAction == .settle and the selected thread is settled, otherwise "\(settings.threadFinishAction.title) thread", i.e. "Settle thread" or "Archive thread"
finishActionSymbol: "arrow.uturn.backward" for a settled thread under .settle, otherwise "checkmark.circle" for .settle and "archivebox" for .archive
Notification bodies: "Waiting for your decision." for an approval, "Finished." for .completed, "Stopped." for .interrupted, "Stopped with an error." for .failed, "" for .running
ProjectFile.symbol SF Symbol map: "test" gives "checkmark.seal", "lint" gives "wand.and.stars", "configure" gives "gearshape", "build" gives "hammer", "debug" gives "ant", anything else gives "play"
Dock badge label: String(unread) when unread > 0, otherwise nil
Animations: Chrome.settleFlight for settle and reopen, Chrome.panelSlide for archive, delete and the finish action
feature_notes: init() coerces every thread whose lastStatus == .running to .interrupted, and every thread whose hydra?.status == .running to .stopped with hydra.finishedAt = .now, because a head at work when the app last quit went with its session
init() clears settings.lastProjectID when that project no longer exists
bootstrap() prefetches the 12 most recently updated non-archived, non-panel threads (prefix(12)) so the first click into a conversation parses no history on the main thread

bootstrap() order: warmDocuments, settings.loadKeychainInBackground, LoginEnvironment.load, sweepHydraCopies (after the login environment so git runs with the user's PATH), resumeHydraMerges, start the 300 second repeating merge sweep, providers.refreshAll, then a TaskGroup loading catalogs for .claude, .codex, .deepseek and .meta when installed, then .zai serially when installed, and finally Storage.sweepOrphanedAttachments() unless WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled
The merge sweep repeats every 300 seconds (5 minutes) for as long as the app runs and skips chats with a turn or head still running

Idle rule: a thread left alone for 600 seconds (10 minutes) gives its agent process back; the loop continues rather than stopping when a turn is still running, otherwise stopSession() then releaseIdleRuntime()

releaseIdleRuntime refuses when there is no runtime, the thread is selected, the thread is a panel child of the selection, the runtime does not hold only persisted state, the id is in sessionsToRelease, autoContinue.resumesAt has an entry for it, the thread has terminal sessions, or runningDroppyHeads(of:) != 0. When it proceeds it calls runtime.saveNow() then runtime.cancelPersistence() before dropping the runtime, so a read that follows waits for the save.

threads(in:) hides archived and in-panel threads, hides a thread whose parent is also shown, then sorts: settled last; among settled by settledFirst (settledAt or updatedAt descending); among unsettled pinned first, then sortOrder ascending, with a nil sortOrder sorting before a non-nil one so threads created after a reorder stay on top, else createdAt descending

moveThread(_:to:placeAfter:) works only within one project, refuses settled threads on either side, makes the moved thread adopt the target's isPinned, and rewrites sortOrder = Double(position); it returns whether the order changed
moveInActivity writes activityOrder = Double(position) and activityOrderDay = Calendar.current.startOfDay(for: thread.updatedAt)
sidebarThreads walks only projects where isExpanded is true and inlines each thread's helpers unless the thread foldsHelpers or isSettled
helpers(of:) returns non-archived children that are not in a panel, except hydra heads which appear even while in a panel, sorted createdAt descending (newest first)
panelHeads(of:) returns in-panel, non-archived hydra heads sorted by hydra.index ascending with nil treated as Int.max, tie-broken by createdAt ascending
panelSubagent(of:) returns the first in-panel, non-archived, non-head child

openThreadOnLaunch reuses the newest unused thread in the current project (same project, not archived, not settled, not a helper, lastStatus == nil, !hasCustomTitle and title == ChatThread.untitled) and refreshes its provider, model, effort, fastMode, hydraPairID and hydraEnabled from a fresh template; a provider change also clears providerSessionID and providerResumeAt. With no such thread it creates one.
currentProject fallback chain: the selected thread's project, then settings.lastProjectID, then the project of the most recently updated non-archived non-panel thread, then projects.first

makeThread precedence: the project's own HydraPair wins over the carried chat, which wins over the last picker pair (settings.lastHydraPairID, or the most recently updated non-helper thread's hydraPairID), which wins over settings.defaultProvider; a provider that is not installed falls back to installed[0]. carriesModel is true only when the project pair has no orchestratorModel and the carried chat is on the same provider; otherwise the model is providers.defaultModel(for:)?.id, the effort is preference.effort ?? settings.lastEffort(for:) and fastMode comes from the model preference.
newThread expands the destination project, remembers it as the last project, selects the new thread, and creates a worktree when (workspace ?? settings.defaultWorkspaceMode) == .worktree

forwardThread awaits the source runtime's ensureLoaded(), re-resolves the thread and project because they can change while history loads, captures a ThreadContinuation from snapshotForPersistence(), and installs it into a new thread titled "Continued: <title>"

moveThread(_:toProject:) stops the session, clears worktreePath, branch, providerSessionID and providerResumeAt, expands the destination project, remembers it, and sets sidebarRevealThreadID so the sidebar scrolls to the moved row
archive cascades to helpers, deselects through selectNeighbor, stops the session, releases the hydra copy, sets isArchived, clears isPinned, resets isSettled and settledAt, and updates the dock badge
unarchive restores the thread and every archived helper whose parentThreadID matches, then updates the dock badge

settle refuses a settled thread or a helper, settles the thread and its helpers with a shared Date.now, clears isPinned and hasUnread, updates the dock badge, plays SettleChime when sounds && settings.settleSound, and writes the library immediately rather than on the debounce
reopen clears isSettled and settledAt, sets updatedAt = .now, clears activityOrder and activityOrderDay, un-settles the children, and saves immediately

finishSelectedThread archives (inside withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide)) when the finish action is .archive or when the thread is a helper; otherwise it posts a FinishRequest and waits 80 milliseconds for a sidebar row to claim it, falling back to reopenAnimated or settleAnimated
settleSelectedThread ignores helpers and uses the same 80 millisecond FinishRequest handshake

askToArchiveSelectedThread deletes outright with no question when the runtime exists and is not loading history, has no turns, no continuation, an empty draft, no followUps and is not running; otherwise it posts an ArchiveRequest and falls back to archive after 80 milliseconds

delete cascades to every child, deselects via selectNeighbor, reports an unfinished hydra head to its lead as .interrupted through finishHydraHead so the batch settles, deletes checkpoints, and removes the worktree only when removeWorktree is true or thread.hydra?.hasOwnCopy == true

deleteArchivedThreads also removes helpers of archived threads, clears the selection if it was among them, deletes all documents in one Storage.deleteDocuments call, removes checkpoints and hydra own-copy worktrees per thread, and leaves ordinary worktrees on disk exactly as a single delete does

spawnSubagent hands the prompt to an existing panel helper rather than making a second one: a running helper gets enqueueFollowUp(text:attachments: []), an idle one gets its draft set and send() called. A new helper inherits the parent's projectID, provider, model, effort, runtimeMode and fastMode, and gets parentThreadID, isInPanel = true, the given title and hasCustomTitle = true. It runs in the project folder itself so a merge lands on the main checkout, never in a thread's worktree.

closeSubagent interrupts a running helper and defers stopSession until the turn finishes by inserting the id into sessionsToRelease, then sets isInPanel = false so the helper moves to the sidebar under its parent

createWorktree refuses when the thread already has a worktree, or when the folder is not a git repository or has no commits (showing the "Worktree unavailable" alert). The path is Storage.worktreesDirectory / "<project name with spaces replaced by '-' and lowercased>-<first 8 chars of the lowercased thread uuid>", the branch is "droppy-code/<the same 8 chars>", based on the current git branch. On success it runs every project script with runOnWorktreeCreate == true in the new directory and shows the terminal.

isOnScreen: true for the selected thread itself; for a child of the selection, true when it is in a panel and not archived; otherwise true only when the child and its parent are not archived, the parent is not in a panel, does not fold helpers and is not settled, matching what SidebarView shows inline

threadNeedsAttention marks the thread read instead of notifying when NSApp.isActive and the thread is on screen; otherwise it notifies with body "Waiting for your decision." and calls NSApp.requestUserAttention(.informationalRequest)

turnFinished writes lastStatus and updatedAt, and sets hasUnread = !isVisible except for hydra heads which never mark themselves; releases a deferred session from sessionsToRelease; returns early when autoContinue.turnFinished took the turn (a spent usage limit waits for the reset with no chime and no error banner); a hydra head reports to its lead via hydraHeadTurnFinished only when continues == false, and returns either way

Chime rule: chimed = settings.chimeWhenFinished && status != .interrupted, so a stop the user asked for is silent. When the chime sounded, the notification is posted with sound: nil so the banner does not double it; otherwise sound: .default
The notification is only posted when the thread is not visible and settings.notifyWhenFinished is true
markRead([UUID]) coalesces many threads into a single library write, so the cells and the sidebar see one change rather than one per thread
notify() is skipped entirely when WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, and skipped when NSApp.isActive and the thread is on screen
requestNotificationPermission asks once (didRequestNotifications) for [.alert, .sound, .badge]
updateDockBadge counts threads where hasUnread && !isArchived && !isInPanel

textEngine: .off returns nil; .claude returns claude(); .codex returns codex(); .automatic returns codex() ?? claude() when the preferred provider is .codex, otherwise claude() ?? codex(). Each engine needs providers.status(kind).auth != .signedOut and a resolved executable; codex additionally needs providers.defaultModel(for: .codex)?.id.
ProjectFile.scripts silently returns [] when droppy-code.json is missing or unparseable, and skips any script entry missing "name" or "command"
unresolved_questions: The Hydra methods used here (hydraPickerPairs, hydraLead(of:for:), sweepHydraCopies, resumeHydraMerges, releaseHydraCopy, runningDroppyHeads, finishHydraHead, hydraHeadTurnFinished, isAnyHydraMergeRunning, hydraHeadsEffort) are declared in another file, so their behavior cannot be established from here
ObservedValue's implementation is not in this file, so its exact observation semantics are taken from the comments rather than from code
hydraHeadRetries is declared here but never read or written in this file; the 'a head gets two more goes' policy lives in the Hydra extension
ChatThread.untitled's literal string, and therefore the exact default thread title, is defined elsewhere
Chrome.settleFlight and Chrome.panelSlide animation curves and durations are defined elsewhere
SwitchLatency.noteSwitch is called with a title or "none" but whether it ships in release builds or is instrumentation only cannot be determined from this file

files.purpose: The complete UserDefaults-backed preferences object for this Mac: it declares the TextGenerationChoice, ThreadFinishAction, SidebarMode and ActivityThreadStyle enums with their exact titles and detail strings, the ModelPin and ModelPreference value types, and an @Observable AppSettings class whose every stored property writes itself back to UserDefaults under an exact key from the private Key enum, plus Keychain-backed API keys for DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai and Command Code, the Hydra pair store, the composer's pinned model list and per-model preferences.

Keychain reads: one round trip per key inside readKeys, either lazily via readKeychainIfNeeded or off the main thread via Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) in loadKeychainInBackground
Migration side effect: once a key is confirmed in the Keychain, the plaintext defaults copy for that provider is removed (removeObject for deepseekAPIKey, metaAPIKey, zaiAPIKey, commandcodeAPIKey)
JSON encode/decode into UserDefaults Data for projectActivationOverrides, modelList, modelPreferences and hydraPairs

macOS Keychain via the provider-specific *Keychain helpers; a comment records that a Keychain query on every render made Settings lag and that two of them before the window existed made launch wait on securityd

SwiftUI Observation (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored) with @MainActor isolation and a nonisolated static readKeys for off-main Keychain reads

feature_notes: threadFinishAction governs the check on a thread row, Shift+Cmd+Delete and the palette's finish action
chatZoom is a step of ChatZoom moved by a slider in the chat's chrome row; the row and the chat box keep their own size
backdropOpacity 0 means clear glass with the desktop showing through, and with a wallpaper set the backdrop is the picture drawn at this same value

sidebarMode is a derived tri-state: the getter returns .column when !sidebarFloats, .panelOnly when sidebarOnlyFloats, otherwise .floating; the setter writes sidebarFloats = (newValue != .column) and sidebarOnlyFloats = (newValue == .panelOnly)

isProjectActive(id) returns projectActivationOverrides[id.uuidString] ?? projectsEnabled; setProjectActive writes an explicit override, clearProjectActivationOverride removes it, hasProjectActivationOverride reports its presence

API key precedence in apiKey(for:): the trimmed Settings value wins, otherwise, when provider.acceptsAPIKey and provider.apiKeyEnvVar exist, the trimmed value of that env var from LoginEnvironment.current. Documented env vars: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY for DeepSeek and MODEL_API_KEY for Meta; Command Code's Studio key is handed to the CLI as COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY and is optional because `cmd login` serves instead.
Documented endpoints in comments: Meta Model API (Muse Spark) at https://api.meta.ai/v1, Z.ai GLM Coding Plan at https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4

Keychain reads are deferred: the four API key input properties start as "" in init and are filled later by loadKeychainInBackground (called from AppModel.bootstrap) or lazily by readKeychainIfNeeded on the first apiKey / apiKeyInput / setAPIKeyInput call. fillKeys guards on didReadKeychain and raises isReadingKeychain so the fill never writes back to the Keychain or to the plaintext fallback.
storeAPIKeyFallback trims the value and removes the defaults entry when it is empty, so a key the Keychain holds never sits in defaults too
updateHydraPair clamps the edited pair's maxHeads through HydraPair.clampedCap and skips the write when the pair is unchanged
hydraPair(for:model:) precedence: a pair on this provider whose orchestratorModel equals the model, else a pair on this provider whose orchestratorModel is nil, else the provider's first pair
addToModelList refuses duplicates and anything past modelListLimit (15)
moveModel computes dest = to + (placeAfter ? 1 : 0), then decrements dest when from < dest, returns false when from == dest, and otherwise removes and reinserts the pin
setPreference stores nil, removing the entry, when the preference equals a default-constructed ModelPreference()
setEnabled always removes the provider rawValue from disabledProviders first, then appends it when enabled == false
setBinaryPath trims whitespace and stores nil for an empty string
hydraPairs decode leniently through Lenient<HydraPair> with compactMap(\.value), so one unreadable pair does not lose the rest

hydraTempersHeadEffort (default true) makes heads think at a working effort rather than the lead's own: a lead above medium sends out medium heads on the same model, and a scale with no medium works out at its middle rung, unless the pair names a head effort

hydraIsolateHeads (default true) gives each Droppy-run head its own copy of the checkout so no head sees another's half-done work; its changes land in the chat's checkout when it reports. Off, the heads work in the checkout itself.
hydraAlwaysHeads sends every user message to a head, sent or queued, idle lead or not, so the lead only hears the heads' reports; when every head is busy a message goes the ordinary way
hydraQueueHeads sends a follow-up queued during a running turn straight to a head instead of waiting for the turn
hydraAutoMerge, when on, sends the team's work out as a merge request once the lead has finished and every head is back, and brings the checkout up to date
hydraReviewHeads makes the lead audit every head's landed work before finishing, reading the files the reports name and correcting what is wrong
hydraAutoPopsHeads gives each head after the first a panel of its own on the left and right while there is room beside the chat (see PanelScene.autoPopped)
showsUsagePanel is set by the General setting, the usage popover's pop-out button and the panel's own close button, so it persists across threads and relaunches
hydraDefaultEnabled is stored under ChatThread.hydraDefaultKey because ChatThread seeds new threads from it before any AppSettings object exists; it is true until the user first switches a chat off
The theme read falls back from the appTheme key to the legacy appearance key before defaulting to .system, and ThemeManager.current is set from the initial value inside init
